ranked.title: EXP-62, sharpened: does transfer price skill on a brain that takes in content, against a committed null?
ranked.milestone: New rung M1b (content validity). Also re-crosses M1 and additive M2 on a multi-step chain, and tests the angle's premise ('a fake that produces the delta had to carry real task-information').
ranked.what:
Rung 0. Do this in the same fire, before the pilot, with no compute: apply the status corrections listed below; log EXP-49/52 plus the content sub-track (EXP-48/53/54/55/58/61) as iter35; replace NEXT ITERATIONS with this list; write the RUN GATE lines.

Rung 1. Merge EXP-52's market (exp/EXP-52_noesis_lite_null_counterfactual.py) with EXP-58's delayed-credit brain and its alone phase run through step. Five changes:
(a) Shared student seeds across teachers. EXP-52's seed base includes TEACHERS.index(kind) (line 69), so every teacher got different students, and the null and untaught twins were rebuilt for every job. Build them once per student instead. That gives a know-k ladder within each student and roughly halves compute.
(b) Price against the stronger counterfactual. Worth = taught minus whichever of {random-label null, untaught} has the higher pooled mean on this instrument. This is a fixed rule, not a per-student max, which would push every price down and make the fake bar easier to pass. Report both counterfactuals.
(c) Window pilot under the exact run conditions: 3 students, lesson lengths 40/80/120, know-1..4 plus random. EXP-58's know-4 is .932 at 120, close to ceiling. At 40 the steps between know-k levels are about .05.
(d) Finalize pay on batches of 6 students per teacher. This replaces EXP-52's two-student > .125 rule, which leaked .209 of pay to fakes.
(e) Log every twin's per-state greedy actions and every teacher's label stream, so items 5 and 6 can run mostly from saved data.

Arms:
- know-1..4;
- random, wrong-chain, echo;
- abstain (this is the untaught twin, so it costs nothing);
- anti-echo: labels uniformly among the 4 actions other than the student's executed mistake. This is one line of code, because the labeller already receives `a` and fires only after executed mistakes (EXP-49 line 63).
ranked.why_now:
This is the binding question, and both lenses and all three readers agree. Each earlier run tested a different combination, and none tested all three conditions together:
- EXP-49 was fooled: against an untaught twin a random fake earned +.179.
- EXP-52 was blind: against the form-matched null, know-4 scored +.013 and Spearman was .06.
- EXP-58/61 found content on only one brain: +.469 (11 SEM) on the delayed-credit brain vs +.016 on the default brain.
That leaves exactly one untested combination: a brain that takes in content, the form-matched null and a known-skill ladder.

Two more reasons:
- EXP-62 has been ready since 10-14 and lost the 10-15 and 10-16 fires to the #202 memory track.
- Every later chain rung reuses this harness.
ranked.cost_days: 1 fire. About 1-2 h of code (merging two existing scripts), about 3 min of pilot, and an estimated 25-35 min full run at 4 workers (72 students x about 10 twins x about 10 s per 120-attempt twin, scaled from EXP-58's 461 s). These are estimates, not measurements.
ranked.ready: Ready. Rung 0 has to land first in the same fire; otherwise the stale list keeps sending the loop to the queue.
ranked.kill_or_confirm:
Pre-register the following.

CONFIRM if all of these hold:
- means are ordered know-1 < know-2 < know-3 < know-4, and pooled Spearman(worth, k) >= .3 (EXP-52's metric, n >= 288);
- know-4 >= .2 against the stronger counterfactual;
- every task-blind fake, abstain included, has mean <= 0;
- fakes take <= .10 of pay.
Then transfer prices skill on an instrument that takes in content, and the angle stands, with the instrument I and the null N named.

KILL (angle refuted under its best conditions): any task-blind fake earns worth >= know-2 with adequate power.

DECISIVE FOR NOESIS WITHOUT KILLING THE ANGLE:
- Content is large but Spearman < .1. Then transfer is a pass/fail filter, not a price.
- Anti-echo is > 0 by 2 SEM. Then the zero point has to be the best fake in a declared, committed class, not uniform noise, because the corrective schedule leaks one elimination bit per mistake to whoever does the labelling.

ranked.title: EXP-62b: does the price among genuine contributions depend on which brain measures it? (absorbs EXP-64)
ranked.milestone: Restated M5 (the instrument I as an outside ingredient) and the instrument axis of M3, which EXP-16 held fixed. Decides whether a worth independent of the instrument exists.
ranked.why_now:
EXP-58 vs EXP-61 already shows that changing only the brain moves measured worth by about .45 (5.8 combined SEM), with the same contributions, task and oracle. If the ORDER of worth also depends on the brain, v(S) is defined only relative to a committed instrument, and whoever picks that instrument sets the price.

After EXP-62 this is the cheapest way to falsify 'v(S) is a property of the contribution'. Folding EXP-64 in turns a 9-minute diagnostic into a comparison that can support a decision.

I chose the early/late design over re-running the know-k ladder on a second brain. On any brain that takes in content, more knowledge giving more transfer is close to forced. The informative question is which knowledge each brain can use.
ranked.cost_days: 1 fire. Small code delta on top of EXP-62. About 15-25 min of compute at 4 workers (estimate).
ranked.ready: Blocked on EXP-62 (the harness and the chosen lesson length). The design is otherwise complete.
ranked.kill_or_confirm:
CONFIRM: on every instrument that takes in content (content > 2 SEM), early-2, late-2 and know-4 come out in the same price order, and the early/late ratio agrees within about 2 SEM. Ordinal worth is then robust to the instrument, and only its scale is set by the instrument.

KILL FOR NOESIS: the early/late order flips significantly between two instruments that both take in content. Then no worth exists independently of the instrument, and I and N must be committed from outside, in advance, just like T.

If B is blind: that is the #198 reading (the actor step alone is not the block), and C carries the comparison. EXP-51 stays parked.

ranked.title: EXP-62c: M3 off the bandit, plus the in-expectation argument from the code
ranked.milestone: M3 (isomorphism-invariance). Moves it from 'empirical on a saturated bandit' toward an argument. Bears on Noesis gate WASH-PROBLEM-INDEX row 9.
ranked.what:
Rung A, about 0.25 day, no compute, can run in any fire (including while EXP-62 computes in the background). Read Brain.compose initialization and the step/act update path. Check two things:
- whether initial weights are exchangeable when input and output units are permuted;
- whether the learning law and the action choice are permutation-equivariant.
Look for argmax tie-breaking toward low indices, biases tied to particular actions, and positional context. If both properties hold, write the short argument that expected paired transfer is invariant under consistent relabeling.

Rung B, 1 fire. Use the EXP-62 harness at a lesson length where learning does not saturate. Apply about 12-20 random consistent permutations of action indices and weather-input order to the chamber, the teachers' labels and the readout together. Same student seeds. Teachers know-2, know-4 and wrong-chain. Paired worth against EXP-62's committed counterfactual.

State explicitly that relabeling the instrument itself is not covered; that is item 2.
ranked.why_now:
EXP-16's limits:
- one permutation per task, not the 8!-element group;
- learning at ceiling, which forces the .500;
- the paired form was chosen after seeing the data.
The 'provably' bar is unmet.

The code read is the only route to an argument, and it costs almost nothing. One plausible invariance breaker is an inference, not measured: the text runs collapsed onto action 0 (EXP-43), which points at index-dependent behaviour.

I ranked this above scale (the value lens had it 6th) because rung A is nearly free, and rung B reuses item 1's harness with no new build.
ranked.cost_days: About 1.25 total: 0.25 day of reading, plus 1 fire of about 25 min compute (estimate).
ranked.ready: Rung A is ready now. Rung B is blocked on EXP-62.
ranked.kill_or_confirm:
CONFIRM: initialization is exchangeable and the learning law is equivariant in the code, and each teacher's worth stays within 2 SEM across all permutations with ranks preserved. M3 then holds in expectation, with a proof sketch.

KILL: a named term breaks the symmetry (index-ordered tie-breaking, or a bias tied to a particular action), and some permutation moves a teacher's worth by more than 3 SEM. Then v(S) needs explicit symmetrization (averaging over a random relabeling committed in advance), and M3 stays open with that term named.

ranked.title: Scale and interference on a brain that takes in content (stale item 4, never run on the transfer harness)
ranked.milestone: M1 'robust across sizes' (currently unshown) and the stale NEXT item 4. Folds in EXP-07 (forgetting).
ranked.what:
Rung A, 1 fire. Extend the chamber from 4 to 6 stages, or add weathers. Run only the RUN GATE window pilot, with know-k and random teachers, on the best instrument from items 1 and 2.

Rung B, 1 fire. Run the full know-k ladder and fakes at the chosen length, under item 1's pre-registered bars. Add a half-life arm: after the lesson, N attempts of unrelated life in a different chamber, then measure worth again.

Optional if rung B has headroom: one non-label channel (per-step grades as in EXP-39).
ranked.why_now:
All of the content evidence on a chain comes from one chamber, one corrective schedule and 24 students per length (EXP-58's stated limits). The first step up from the bandit is what exposed the instrument problem (EXP-49), so the next step up must run only on a brain already shown to take in content.

This is the only path to the 'robust across sizes' half of M1. It can kill: if content does not carry across tasks, Noesis would have to validate its instrument per task class.

I placed it above the M5 curve because most of M5's new information can be derived at zero compute (see item 5).
ranked.cost_days: 2 fires (build and pilot, then run). Estimate.
ranked.ready: Needs design (the chamber extension). Blocked on EXP-62 passing at least its content and know-4 bars.
ranked.kill_or_confirm: CONFIRM: the know-k ranking and fakes <= 0 hold at 6 stages (Spearman >= .3), and worth keeps >= .5 of its lesson-end value after the unrelated life. KILL: ranking or fake pricing collapses as the chain gets longer, so the measure is valid only on short chains. Or worth decays to noise under ordinary continuing life, so transfer has to be measured immediately; that shapes the protocol's settlement window.

ranked.title: M5 on the chain: a measured capture curve with an adversary that chooses which tasks it supplies
ranked.milestone: M5 (exogenous anchor), restated as T + I + N.
ranked.what:
Rung 0, no compute; can ride in item 1's rung 0. Add a derived caveat to M5-EXOGENOUS-ANCHOR.md. In EXP-17's own linear model, genuine and fake differ only on contexts where R disagrees with T.
- With a uniform adversary pool, both terms scale by (1 - a_R), so on a saturated learner q* = .5 for EVERY a_R. A bandit sweep over a_R alone therefore cannot move q*.
- If the adversary supplies only states where R disagrees with T, the same model gives q* = (1 - a_R)/(2 - a_R): .33 at a_R .5 and .20 at a_R .75.
This is derived, not measured. It applies only to an adversary that knows T well enough to find the states where its rule disagrees, which a deliberately built fake does (EXP-52's wrong-chain is built from c.right()).

Rung 1, 1 fire. On item 1's harness and saved per-state logs, add consistent partial-rule teachers that agree with T on m of 4 stages (m = 1, 2, 3). Compute paired genuine-minus-adversary worth as a function of q under two pools: a uniform adversary pool, and a disagreement-selecting adversary pool. The only new compute is the partial-rule arms.
ranked.why_now:
EXP-17's own reflection admits q* = .500 is forced by the design. The derivation shows the stated boundary ('an honest majority of tasks') is an upper bound on q*. That changes the task-supply bond Noesis would need.

The chain run checks whether the linear model survives learning that does not saturate. This is also Boardy's round-3 ask.

It ranks below items 1-4 because answering it helps every approach equally, and most of its value is captured by the zero-compute rung.
ranked.cost_days: 0.1 day (rung 0) plus 1 fire (about 20 min of new compute plus analysis; estimate).
ranked.ready: Rung 0 is ready now. Rung 1 is blocked on EXP-62's per-state logs.
ranked.kill_or_confirm:
CONFIRM (a useful boundary): measured q* tracks the derived curve. A disagreement-selecting adversary flips prices well below .5 (around .33 at a_R .5), and a uniform one at about .5. The honest task share Noesis must guarantee is then about 1/(2 - a_R), not one half. Write that into M5 as a design number.

SURPRISE: q* on the chain sits far from both predictions. The linear model then does not describe a learner below saturation, and M5 must cite the measured curve only.

ranked.title: Interior battery on the label streams, post hoc (makes M2's 'wash_sim adversary' literal)
ranked.milestone: M2 (feature-matched fake). The program currently says 'ported from wash_sim.rs', which is not literally true.
ranked.why_now:
This is the cheapest thing that moves M2. It replaces the 1-2 day port of novelty, synergy, cycle-energy and circulation onto EXP-10, whose interior is identical by construction, so that port would show little.

It also answers, more cheaply, the key question a learned v(S) would raise: can label-stream features separate fakes? It polishes a rung that is already crossed, so it ranks below the open questions.
ranked.ready: Blocked on EXP-62 having run with label streams logged (change (e) in item 1).
ranked.kill_or_confirm:
CONFIRM (the impossibility core on a second substrate): every interior feature ranks at least one fake at or above the genuine teachers, while transfer orders them correctly. For example, echo has total agreement and wrong-chain has perfect consistency.

SURPRISE: some interior feature separates. That does not break the core, because these fakes were not built to match that feature. It does make 'a fake matched on that feature' the next adversary to build before claiming M2 against wash_sim's adversary.

ranked.title: EXP-05: does a mid-lesson snapshot of the delayed-credit brain replay bit-identically in a fresh process, on main and on the #203 head?
ranked.milestone: Instrument infrastructure. A precondition for committing I so that any validator can replay the twin.
ranked.what: Snapshot a delayed-credit brain partway through a lesson and restore it in a fresh process. Check that it continues bit-identically and that the digests match. Do this on main (6499e56) and on the PR #203 worktree (~/_cadence_203, 9a2d422, checkpoint format cadence-generic/9).
ranked.why_now: A verifiable v(S) needs any validator to replay the same twin and get the same delta. Same-process twins are shown: EXP-08 is bit-identical across versions and on the #203 head. Restoring the brain that carries content in a fresh process is not shown, and #203 changes the checkpoint format. The worktree already exists, so running both now covers the merge.
ranked.cost_days: 0.1-0.25. Filler for any fire whose main item is blocked or running in the background.
ranked.kill_or_confirm: CONFIRM: continuation is bit-identical on both, so the instrument can be committed and replayed. KILL: the runs diverge (RNG or replay state not captured). Measured transfer then cannot be verified independently until upstream fixes it; file an upstream issue with the minimal repro.

frontier:
2026-10-16 (re-rank, no new rung): no milestone has moved since iter13 (10-09).

Status on the bandit:
- M1 and additive M2 are crossed.
- M4 is crossed, but its immunity to coordination holds by construction.
- M3 is empirical only: one permutation per task, learning saturated.
- M5 is a boundary whose q* = .5 is set by the symmetric design.

Off the bandit, the measure failed its first richer substrate:
- Against an untaught twin, a random-label fake earned +.179 (EXP-49).
- Against a form-matched null, fakes priced at or below 0, but skill was invisible on the default brain: know-4 +.013, Spearman .06 (EXP-52).
- Content reaches only the delayed-credit brain: +.469, 11 SEM (EXP-58), vs +.016 on the default brain (EXP-61).

So v(S) depends on the instrument I and the null N, not only the task T. The binding open question is whether transfer prices skill on a brain that takes in content, against a committed null. That is EXP-62: ready since 10-14, not yet run.

loop_policy:
Every scheduled loop fire goes to a program rung.

When the program counts as blocked:
- Only when every open NEXT ITERATIONS item is written down as blocked on a named, Will-gated decision.
- A stale or exhausted list does not count. In that case the fire re-ranks first (no compute), then runs the new top item.
- Add a staleness check to cron-prompts/cadence-experiment-loop.md: if NEXT ITERATIONS was ordered more than 3 days ago, or its top item is done, re-rank before choosing.
- This closes the leak that sent the loop to the queue. The 10-08 list read as blocked, and side tracks had filled the queue's 'ready' slots.

When teaching, memory (#202) and text runs happen:
- On Will's explicit in-session ask, or as a second run in a fire whose program rung is already running in the background with cores to spare (4 workers total on the box).
- They are tagged by track, and they do not take iteration numbers.

How follow-ups enter the queue:
- Follow-ups spawned by off-program runs enter as 'candidate', not 'ready'. Side tracks then cannot refill the fallback queue on their own.
- Any run that prices contributions by transfer (every Noesis-lite run) is on-program by definition and goes in the program log.

Target split:
- At least 3 of every 4 loop fires on program rungs until EXP-62, 62b and the M3 run are done.
- Audit the split weekly by wall time, not run count. From 10-09 to 10-16, v(S) got about 7-8% of wall time, or 19% counting prerequisites.

The memory track has real upstream value. Will can buy it explicitly, but it should not take program fires by default.
drop_or_park: FOLD: standalone EXP-64 becomes instrument B in EXP-62b. Its #198 reading comes out of that run.

DROP: the EXP-17 asymmetric sweep on the bandit, with only a_R varied. Under EXP-17's own linear model with a uniform adversary pool and saturated learning, q* = .5 for every a_R, so the run cannot move it. Replaced by the derived (1 - a_R)/(2 - a_R) caveat now, and by the chain capture curve (item 5).

DROP: the 'self-sharpen' fake. On this schedule labels fire only after executed mistakes, so labelling the student's greedy action mostly reproduces echo. It would also need the student's policy, which the labeller signature (c, a) does not carry. Anti-echo replaces it.

PARK: an 'eliminator' fake that remembers rejected actions per state. It learns the task from the student's own failures, which makes it a relay rather than a fake that never sees the task. Whether reprocessing the receiver's own feedback should be paid is a design decision to make before running it.

PARK: learned v(S) trained on transfer labels. The labels come from the chamber's own oracle, not exogenous realized use, so this does not advance irreducible 2 as stated. rationale:
Both lenses and all three readers agree on the core. Does twin-ablation transfer read content or perturbation, and against which instrument and null? EXP-62 is the test. The program file's stale list, not the compute budget, is what kept it from running. I checked the load-bearing numbers in the files: EXP-58 (+.469 at 120, random -.078 vs untaught), EXP-61 (+.016, a gap of .45 at 5.8 combined SEM), EXP-52 (know-4 +.013, Spearman .06 at n=288, fakes .209 of pay) and EXP-17's reflection that q* = .5 is forced.

Disagreements, decided:

(1) The program-file repair is rung 0 of EXP-62, in the same fire, not a separate ranked item. Both lenses require it before launch, and its exact edits are listed under status corrections.

(2) EXP-64 folds into EXP-62b, as the decisive lens proposed. For the second instrument I took the decisive lens's early-2 / late-2 / know-4 design over the value lens's re-run of the know-k ladder. On any brain that takes in content, more knowledge giving more transfer is close to forced, so the informative question is which knowledge each brain can use. Instrument C must be fixed before any data. I verified the value lens's correction: the delayed-credit brain came from EXP-45's pre-registered key-door point and was confirmed by EXP-58, not chosen for separating. Any new instrument must keep that discipline.

(3) Baseline. The decisive lens's catch is real: against the random-label null alone, a teacher who sends nothing earns about +.08, the mirror of EXP-49's hole. I adopted a stronger-counterfactual baseline, but as a fixed rule on pooled means, not a per-student max, which would bias prices down and flatter the fake bar.

(4) Adaptive fake. Anti-echo (value lens) beats self-sharpen (decisive lens). The labeller already receives the executed mistake and fires only after mistakes (EXP-49 line 63), so anti-echo is one line, whereas self-sharpen roughly reproduces echo on this schedule and needs the student's policy.

(5) Lesson length. I chose the window pilot at 40/80/120 over a fixed 120, because know-4 is .932 at 120 and the RUN GATE requires a pilot anyway.

(6) EXP-17. The decisive lens is right that a bandit sweep over a_R is uninformative, and the reason is sharper than either lens stated. With a uniform adversary pool, both terms scale by (1 - a_R), so q* = .5 for every a_R. What moves q* is which states the adversary supplies. The same model gives q* = (1 - a_R)/(2 - a_R) for an informed adversary that picks disagreement states: .33 at a_R .5. This is derived, not measured, but it corrects M5's 'honest majority' at zero compute, and the chain run should measure it.

(7) Order of the middle of the list. M3 goes third (the decisive lens's position): the code read is nearly free and can run during EXP-62's compute. Scale goes fourth, above M5, because scale can kill the angle's generality, while most of M5's new information comes from the derivation.
